body:
Tracks the splits required by [`knowledge/decisions/each-machine-has-its-own-machine-crate.md`](https://github.com/emu198x/emu198x/blob/main/knowledge/decisions/each-machine-has-its-own-machine-crate.md) (RULES.md rule 34). Direction from Steve, 2026-10-26: a machine is distinct whenever its hardware differs from the others in its family, however subtly. That includes PAL/NTSC boards (chip, crystal, strap or diode) and different board layouts. The RAM fitted on the same board, a ROM revision, the case and add-ons stay profiles. Families still share a runtime and ship as one emulator, so this changes machine crates, not binaries.

The table is taken from what each crate's own model and region enums say differs. Rows marked **check** need the hardware confirmed against `reference/` before splitting.

| Machine crate | Machines it holds today | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| Dragon 32, Dragon 64, CoCo 1 and CoCo 2 owners | **Split complete:** four fixed owners over common wiring, preserving original v2 states and profiles; real CoCo BASIC/keyboard checks and separate board evidence | #2138 / #2199 |
| Nine named MSX board owners | **Split complete:** six MSX1 and three MSX2 manufacturer boards over common wiring; generic presets retired, nine named v10 saves preserved. HB-10P accuracy remains #2200 | #2139 / #2201 |
| Nine fixed Sega board owners | **Split complete:** late/early/SMS II NTSC/PAL, Japanese SMS, Mark III and Game Gear over common wiring; original v10 saves preserved | #2140 / #2197 |
| DMG, Pocket, SGB, SGB2, CGB and AGB | Complete: six fixed machine owners over `common-nintendo-game-boy`; DMG0 remains a firmware profile. SGB/SGB2 retain limited Game Boy execution (#326); AGB is CGB-only. Original v4/v3 saves preserved | #2141 / #2196 |
| `machine-acorn-bbc-micro`, `machine-acorn-bbc-micro-b-plus`, `machine-acorn-bbc-master-128` | **Split complete:** Model B, B+ and Master 128, with common wiring and family runtime | #2142 / #2195 |
| Four fixed C64 configuration owners | **Implemented configurations split:** breadbin PAL/NTSC and C64C PAL/NTSC over `common-commodore-c64`; exact v22 continuations and seven exclusive tests each. Restore keeps the live Ultimate interface and rejects malformed memory atomically. **Still check:** PCB revisions, early NTSC VIC and CIA date-code populations | #2218 |
| `machine-commodore-c128-pal`, `machine-commodore-c128-ntsc` | **Implemented configurations split:** two fixed VIC-IIe/clock owners over `common-commodore-c128`; exact v22 continuations and seven exclusive tests each. Real BASIC/typed-input and 40/80-column boot evidence retained. C128D and other chip fittings remain unqualified; C64 mode, 2 MHz execution and media hardware remain unimplemented | #2218 |
| `machine-commodore-vic-20-ntsc`, `machine-commodore-vic-20-pal` | **Split complete:** NTSC (6560) and PAL (6561), with shared common wiring and family runtime | #2193 |
| Three fixed PET board owners | **Implemented configurations split:** 32K 2001N/3032 discrete video, graphics-keyboard 4032 and business-keyboard 8032 over `common-commodore-pet`; matching firmware/video correction, exact v5 continuations and seven exclusive tests each. V4 rejects before decode; full PET family coverage remains open | #2219 / #355 |

The A500+ onboard RTC now decodes without slow RAM. Approved v67 saves explicitly read v66, changing only the legacy A500+ RTC-presence flag while retaining clock history; other payloads change only their header. PCB/chip populations and IDE/PCMCIA qualification remain open; exact ECS browser embeds await a supporting published player | #2230 |
| `machine-commodore-amiga-a1200-pal`, `machine-commodore-amiga-a1200-ntsc` | **Implemented configurations split:** fixed regional owners over shared AGA wiring; original v66 saves and exact progressive/interlaced continuations retained, seven exclusive tests each. Fixed resampler coefficients preserve cross-host history. **Still check:** PCB revisions and chip populations. A1200 browser embeds remain disabled for the published A500-only constructor | #2226 |
| `machine-amstrad-cpc464`, `machine-amstrad-cpc664`, `machine-amstrad-cpc6128` | **Implemented configurations split:** fixed owners over common wiring; original v4 saves and first-field output retained, seven exclusive direct tests each; restore/reset firmware and media caches repaired. **Still check:** other Gate Array/CRTC revisions, regional boards and manufacturer-ID links; the HD6845S/generic Gate Array baseline does not qualify them | #2216 |

Individual board implementation remains open | Primary audit stevehill1981/198x#291; metadata merged in #2222 |

Each owner has five exclusive passing tests | #2203 |

Five exclusive fixture-free tests per owner | #2204 / #2206 |
| `machine-nintendo-nes-ntsc`, `machine-nintendo-nes-pal` | **Regional split complete:** fixed NTSC/PAL owners over common wiring; profiles/aliases and corrected v3 saves retained, seven exclusive direct tests each. V2 is rejected because state was missing. **Still check:** distinct Famicom boards, built-in controls and expansion audio; legacy FDS compatibility does not establish a Famicom owner | #2214 / #2213 |

Seven exclusive tests per owner and six exact original v1 continuations. Approved v2 saves retain IPL without a cartridge; loaded v1 states remain readable, blank v1 states reject. Specific PCB/chip populations and CIC remain unqualified; original-software qualification is still open | #2221 |
| `machine-sega-mega-drive-japan`, `machine-sega-genesis`, `machine-sega-mega-drive-europe` | **Split complete:** three fixed market/video owners over common wiring; profile aliases, original v2 states, native/PBC output and held controls preserved. Six exclusive direct tests per owner | #2208 |
| `machine-sega-sg-1000` | **Split complete for three implemented configurations:** NTSC, PAL and early TMS9918 SG-II now have fixed owners, each with seven passing direct tests. PAL uses independent CPU/VDP clocks and v6 saves; v5 NTSC/early-II continuations remain exact, while v5 PAL saves are rejected. Later TMS9118/custom-VDP board populations remain unqualified; browser embeds await the corrected published module | #2143 / merged #2222 / fixed #2223; primary audit stevehill1981/198x#291 |

| `machine-sord-m5-ntsc`, `machine-sord-m5-pal` | **Split complete:** NTSC and PAL, with shared `common-sord-m5` and family runtime | #2187 |
| `machine-spectravideo-svi-328-ntsc`, `machine-spectravideo-svi-328-pal` | **Split complete:** NTSC and PAL, with shared common wiring and family runtime | #2191 |
| `machine-timex-tc2068`, `machine-timex-ts2068` | **Split complete:** fixed PAL TC2068 and NTSC TS2068 owners over `common-timex-2068`; corrected v17 saves, profiles, firmware IDs and held-key/tape continuation preserved. Seven exclusive direct tests per owner; real-ROM BASIC boot qualification remains #52 | #2211 |
| `machine-oric-atmos` | **Scope corrected:** both implemented 48K Oric-1/Atmos profiles have 64 KiB physical DRAM with ROM over the upper 16 KiB. Product names do not establish every PCB/circuit revision. The manufacturer identifies a separate 16K PCB, not currently emulated. Revision mapping remains open | Primary audit stevehill1981/198x#291; metadata merged in #2222 |

### Amiga

The `-ocs` / `-ecs` grouping doesn't match the hardware. Commodore's *Amiga Release 2 Getting Started* (1991, `reference/by-system/commodore-amiga/1991-amiga-release-2-getting-started.txt`) calls the 8372A "ECS Agnus (1 Meg Chip)", used in "later A500s, A2000s", and gives ECS Denise 8373 to the A3000 alone at the 2.0 release. Later A500s and A2000s are mixed: ECS Agnus, OCS Denise 8362.

- **A2000: three boards, all with OCS Denise 8362.** From the A2000's own documents (stevehill1981/198x#279):

  | Board | Agnus | Source |
  |---|---|---|
  | Early German A2000 | DIP 8367 at U58 (8361 for NTSC per the 1991 table) | Commodore Deutschland, *Amiga 2000 Technical Manual*, 3/87 |
  | PCB 312720-01 | Fat Agnus 8370 NTSC / 8371 PAL at U101 | *A2000 System Schematics*, PN 314135-01 |
  | A2000CR, PCB 312720 rev 6.0 (`-05` NTSC, `-06` PAL) | Super Agnus 8372 at U101 | *A2000 System Schematics rev 6*, PN 314135-02, 1989 |

  Only the rev 6.0 board is modelled: `A2000OcsPal`/`Ntsc` fit the 8372A, configured for 1 MiB chip RAM, despite the `-ocs` names. The rev 6 board **ships jumpered for 1 MiB chip RAM**, so the profile is right: "A2000 REV 6 PCB COMES JUMPERED FOR 1 MEG" (Commodore, *Amiga: An Update for the Service Technician*, issue 25, 1989, item 25/3-2.1). Jumper J101 gives the Agnus A19 instead of A23. An older A2000 upgraded with an 8372 is a further variant: it needs J101 moved, the J500 trace cut and, for PAL, J102 opened. Without those it addresses only 512K and runs only NTSC (stevehill1981/198x#280). The source comment calling the early board "Rev A (early Agnus 8371)" mixes up two boards: the German one had the DIP 8367, and the 8371 is on PCB 312720-01.
- **A500: two boards.** Rev 5 carries the 8370 with 256K×1 DRAMs; rev 6a carries the 8372 with 256K×4 DRAMs. Commodore jumpered both to the same 512K chip layout, called them "functionally interchangeable", and did not support the 1 MB mode (*A500 Service Manual*, PN 314981-04, 1990). They are still different hardware under rule 34. The stock and A501 profiles fit the earlier Agnus.
- **The "maxed" A500 is a modification, not an add-on.** It fits the 8372A with 1 MiB chip RAM: a rev 6a board with the unsupported 1 MB jumper. Decide whether it stays a profile of the rev 6a machine.
- **Not modelled yet, so not in the table:** the A3000, the first full-ECS machine (8372B and 8373, #110), and the A4000, which is AGA (#111). The CDTV (#115) and CD32 (#116) are in the same position.

The chip-generation table in `reference/by-system/commodore-amiga/amiga-custom-chips-reference.md` filed the 8372A under OCS. That is corrected in stevehill1981/198x#278, and the A2000 boards are recorded in #279 there.

Already one machine per crate: the Spectrum models, Pentagon, Scorpion, TC2048, Acorn Atom (RAM fitted), Electron (Plus 3 is an add-on), Jupiter Ace (RAM packs), MTX (RAM fitted), Tatung Einstein, Neo Geo AES, and the 1541, 1571 and 1581 drives.

Each split also adds a `machine_id` to `systems.toml`, so the evidence and the Code198x gap report count the machine on its own.

**Sequencing:** waits for the current family release, which includes publishing every unpublished Emu198x and Format198x crate (Steve, 2026-10-26). Each split adds crates to publish. **Approved exceptions:** Sord was approved on 2026-10-28 (#2187); ColecoVision and SVI-328 were approved on 2026-10-29 before release #2170. #2188 completes ColecoVision and #2191 completes SVI-328 under the [approved plan](https://github.com/emu198x/docs/blob/main/plans/2026-10-29-regional-board-splits.md). VIC-20 was also explicitly approved on 2026-10-29 before #2170; #2193 completes VIC-20 under the [VIC-20 plan](https://github.com/emu198x/docs/blob/main/plans/2026-10-29-svi-restored-media-and-vic20-boards.md). These are private workspace splits with no registry publication. On 2026-10-29, we also approved the BBC (#2142), Game Boy (#2141), Game Gear/SMS (#2140), MSX (#2139) and Dragon/CoCo (#2138) splits under the [five-family plan](https://github.com/emu198x/docs/blob/main/plans/2026-10-29-bus-rule-and-five-family-splits.md). #2195 completes BBC, #2196 completes Game Boy and #2197 completes Game Gear/SMS and #2199 completes Dragon/CoCo and #2201 completes MSX. All five approved family splits are complete. #2202 completes the subsequent ZX80, ZX81/TS1000, Atari 2600 and Atari 7800 continuation under the [next regional plan](https://github.com/emu198x/docs/blob/main/plans/2026-10-29-next-regional-board-splits.md). #2203 completes the 2026-10-30 XL/XE continuation under the [XL/XE plan](https://github.com/emu198x/docs/blob/main/plans/2026-10-30-atari-xl-xe-board-owners.md). #2204 completes the subsequent Aquarius NTSC/PAL continuation under the [Aquarius plan](https://github.com/emu198x/docs/blob/main/plans/2026-10-30-aquarius-board-owners.md). #2208 completes the three-market Mega Drive continuation under the [Mega Drive plan](https://github.com/emu198x/docs/blob/main/plans/2026-10-30-mega-drive-board-owners.md). #2210 first fixes Spectrum-family save fidelity with the approved v17/v16-rejection contract; #2211 then completes the TC2068/TS2068 continuation under the [Timex split plan](https://github.com/emu198x/docs/blob/main/plans/2026-10-30-timex-2068-board-owners.md) and [fidelity plan](https://github.com/emu198x/docs/blob/main/plans/2026-10-30-timex-snapshot-fidelity.md). #2214 completes the subsequent NES NTSC/PAL continuation under the [NES plan](https://github.com/emu198x/docs/blob/main/plans/2026-10-30-nes-regional-board-owners.md), with the explicitly approved v3/v2-rejection fix for #2213 first. #2216 completes the subsequent CPC464/CPC664/CPC6128 continuation under the [CPC plan](https://github.com/emu198x/docs/blob/main/plans/2026-10-31-cpc-board-owners.md), preserving v4 saves and fixing restored reset caches before splitting. #2217 completes the subsequent Atari ST continuation under the [Atari ST plan](https://github.com/emu198x/docs/blob/main/plans/2026-10-31-atari-st-board-owners.md), preserving v1 saves and their external-TOS contract. #2218 completes the subsequent six-configuration C64/C128 continuation under the [Commodore plan](https://github.com/emu198x/docs/blob/main/plans/2026-10-31-commodore-regional-board-owners.md), preserving v22 saves and the shared generic family runtime. Other rows retain the existing sequencing.




## Triage — 2026-10-27

Keep as the finite board-split tracker with #2138–#2143 and further unfiled rows. The current shared crates remain, so this is not completed by extraction into repositories. Source-check each check-marked hardware identity before splitting; same-board RAM fit/ROM/case/add-ons remain profiles while real board/chip/crystal/strap differences get machines. Shared family runtimes and shipped binaries remain allowed.
